newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-CHANG KILLS OFF BRITAIN'S GRAND SLAM DREAM.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-CHANG KILLS OFF BRITAIN'S GRAND SLAM DREAM.

text.p: Britain's brightest tennis star in decades, Tim Henman, came crashing back to earth on Friday when he lost in straight sets to American Michael Chang in the third round of the Australian Open.

Henman came on court carrying the burden of a nation hoping that the tall right-hander could be another Fred Perry in the making. But he folded under the pressure before his Union Jack-waving fans had time to warm their seats.
In a match lasting only 104 minutes, second-seeded Chang produced every shot in his considerable repertoire, outclassing the serve-and-volley specialist 6-1 7-6 6-3.
The American, who has not taken a grand slam title since winning the French Open as a 17-year-old in 1989, simply ran down everything Henman could offer.
"I had a bad day at the office, I'm not going to look into it any more than that," said Henman, who soared to 14 in the world rankings after winning his first professional title last week.
"I can't complain with the way I've been playing or the performances up until this...I put in a bad performance, it's as simple as that," he told reporters.

Chang will now meet another player who is running hot, Andrei Medvedev of the Ukraine who took only 70 minutes to beat Dennis van Scheppingen of the Netherlands and then handed his next opponents a warning.
"They should know that they will have to struggle, that they will have to bleed," he said.
In the women's draw, top seed Steffi Graf survived a scare for the second time in the tournament but came from 1-4 down in the first set to beat Argentine Ines Gorrochategui 7-5 6-3.

Graf confirmed that she was helping tennis authorities with an investigation into allegations that she received appearance money against tour rules for playing in tournaments in Germany. She could face a three-month ban from the game.
Another former champion was all smiles. Born in Canada, based in the United States and playing for France, Mary Pierce had Australia on her side when she met Marketa Kochta on an outside show court.
The match itself took a mere 48 minutes, Pierce calmly disposing of the German 6-0 6-2 to underline her comeback from long-running morale and injury problems.

Pierce's next opponent will be fifth seed Anke Huber of Germany, who lost in last year's final to Monica Seles and was beaten by Pierce in the fourth round in 1995. Huber beat Natasha Zvereva of Belarus 7-5 6-0.
Spain's Carlos Moya, who beat defending champion Boris Becker in a first-round upset, made short work of Germany's Bernd Karbacher, winning 6-2 6-2 6-2.
Moya joins two other Spaniards in the fourth round -- men's 14th seed Felix Mantilla and women's third seed Conchita Martinez both won their third-round ties on Friday.
Three other Spaniards -- men's 10th seed Albert Costa, 16th seed Alberto Berasategui and women's number two Arantxa Sanchez Vicario -- play third-round matches on Saturday.
